properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued October 22 at 10:00AM PDT until October 22 at 10:45AM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
SVRLOX

The National Weather Service in OXNARD has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Southern Los Angeles County in southwestern California...

* Until 1045 AM PDT.

* At 959 AM PDT, a severe thunderstorm was located over Carson, or
near Torrance, moving north at 25 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts. Small chance for a brief, weak tornado.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Alhambra...
Downtown Los Angeles...
Griffith Park...
Eagle Rock...
Glendale...
Commerce...
Montebello...
Boyle Heights...
Monterey Park...
Atwater Village...
Highland Park...
Echo Park...
San Gabriel...
Elysian Park...
Downey...
Pico Rivera...
El Monte...
Watts...
East Los Angeles...
and Temple City.
properties.instruction:
Remain alert for a possible tornado! Tornadoes can develop quickly
from severe thunderstorms. If you spot a tornado go at once into the
basement or small central room in a sturdy structure.

For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

Large hail, damaging wind, and continuous cloud to ground lightning
are occurring with this storm. Move indoors immediately. Lightning is
one of nature's leading killers. Remember, if you can hear thunder,
you are close enough to be struck by lightning.

Torrential rainfall is occurring with this storm, and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 22 at 10:44AM MDT until October 23 at 11:00PM MDT by NWS Rapid City SD
properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT FROM 11 AM TO 11 PM MDT FRIDAY DUE TO
GUSTY WINDS AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY FOR NORTHERN CAMPBELL, SOUTHERN
CAMPBELL, CROOK COUNTY PLAINS, AND WESTON COUNTY PLAINS...

.Warm temperatures, humidities as low as 13%, and southwest winds
gusting to 50 mph ahead of an approaching cold front will create
widespread critical fire weather conditions Friday afternoon through
Friday evening. Southwest winds increase over northeastern Wyoming
after 10 am Friday morning with sustained winds of 25 to 35 mph and
gusts of 40 to 50 mph through the afternoon. Winds will shift to the
northwest after midnight as the front moves through. While some
showers may accompany the front, not expecting any widespread wetting
rains.

The National Weather Service in Rapid City SD has issued a Red Flag
Warning in effect from 11 AM to 11 PM MDT Friday.

* TIMING...From 11 AM to 11 PM MDT Friday.

* WINDS...Southwest winds 25 to 35 mph with gusts up to 50 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 13 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions are
either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of strong winds,
low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can contribute to
extreme fire behavior.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Significant coastal flooding expected. Water levels 5 to
7 feet above the normal high tide line expected for Hooper Bay.
Water levels 2 to 4 feet above the normal high tide line for
the rest of the Yukon Delta Coast.

* WHERE...Yukon Delta Coast, particularly Hooper Bay.

* WHEN...From 4 AM Friday to 10 PM AKDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...In Hooper Bay, beach property, and the lowest
buildings will be inundated. The access roads to the airstrip
and the larger parts of town will likely be inundated and access
to the airstrip will be cut off. Elsewhere along the Yukon Delta
Coastline, beach property and the lowest lying roads may be
threatened. Water levels will peak around midday Friday in
Hooper Bay then drop during the afternoon. Be aware that water
levels will remain high during each high tide into the weekend.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Water levels peak with the high tides
Friday and then slowly decrease through the weekend. South to
southeast winds peak Friday with gusts up to 65 mph possible.
properties.instruction: Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property.

scattered thunderstorms across a broad portion of Ventura and Los
Angeles Counties. Movement of this activity was northeast at 30 mph.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 22 at 10:26AM MDT until October 23 at 10:00PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Grand Junction CO has issued a
Flood Warning for the following rivers in Colorado...

San Juan River at Pagosa Springs affecting Archuleta County.

For the San Juan River...including Pagosa Springs...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...San Juan River at Pagosa Springs.

* WHEN...From this afternoon to Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 13.7 feet, Flooding of some residences near the river
around Pagosa Springs is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:00 AM MDT Thursday the stage was 8.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 8.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise above flood stage late this
afternoon to 13.8 feet tomorrow morning. It will then fall below
flood stage tomorrow afternoon to 8.3 feet Saturday afternoon. It
will rise to 8.4 feet early Sunday morning. It will then fall
again and remain below flood stage.
- Flood stage is 10.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/gjt.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at midnight MDT.

possible.
